text:
brightline-sre: Hi team — mid-day traffic spike from Brightline caused sustained TPS > configured SLO. We hit 429s for ~40s, customers reporting degraded UX. Requesting help, this is on Dedicated pool ridge-3-us-east-1 (pool id: ded-78f3).

jessica: sorry you're seeing that — can you paste the error payloads and approximate timeframe? do you know if burst credits were used? :raised_hands:

brightline-sre: sending logs (copied). most responses are 429 with body: {"error":"throttled_admission_control", "reason":"burst_credit_depleted"}. timeframe ~2024-11-01T16:12:34Z - 16:13:20Z. Traffic pattern: short, very high fanout from marketing event.

jessica: got it. @ravi can you pull autoscale and admission control events for ded-78f3? also can we confirm their burst_credit balance and configured headroom?

deploy-bot: autoscale-event ded-78f3: scale_up start=2024-11-01T16:11:50Z end=2024-11-01T16:12:30Z delta=+2 workers. current_workers=6 -> 8. average_scale_latency=38s.

ravi: looking now. admission_control logs show repeated "drop: reason=burst_credit_depleted" starting 16:12:10Z. Burst credits for customer were at 0. Configured headroom is 20% (min_workers=6, target_util=70%).

emma: attaching quick metrics snapshot: GPU_util per-host peaked 93%, avg token_inflight per-host 12k, queue_depth spiked to 480 across pool. tokens/s aggregate ~1200 during peak (normal target ~400). Looks like autoscaler reacted but scale latency + high per-GPU util meant admission control started rejecting. Suspect either headroom too small or noisy neighbor consuming available tokens.

luke: noisy neighbor? any pod-level breakdown?
emma: yes — host ded-78f3-node-04 shows a single tenant (brightline key) consuming 78% of that host's tokens/s. others were at single-digit relative consumption.

jessica: ok so root cause: burst traffic exceeded burst credits and autoscale couldn't add capacity fast enough -> admission control dropped excess requests.

brightline-sre: is there a short-term mitigation we can enable? customers are still reporting errors.

ravi: short term options: 1) temporarily increase burst_credit allotment for Brightline (fast, requires billing change or manually applying internal override) 2) change admission_control policy to allow temporary overcommit for that key (risky) 3) route overflow to hosted fallback models via routing policy if Brightline is on Dedicated + Hosted failover enabled.

luke: quick safe play: enable routing to hosted fallback with model variant rdl-medium-fallback (lower cost, lower latency but keeps UX alive). I'll prepare route change.

billing-bot: note — increasing customer's burst credits above their committed amount requires approval. If we apply internal trial credits, we must flag for postmortem billing reconciliation.

emma: parallel: recommend increasing configured headroom to 40% for this pool and setting faster scale aggression for marketing traffic windows. autoscaler config snippet suggestion: ```json
{
  "scale_policy": "aggressive",
  "target_util": 60,
  "min_headroom_pct": 40,
  "scale_cooldown_seconds": 20
}
``` Apply as canary to ded-78f3 for next scheduled campaign.

jessica: documented repro steps for SRE team: 1) replay traffic trace from 16:11->16:14 at 2x throughput 2) confirm autoscale latency 3) confirm admission_control drops show reason=burst_credit_depleted 4) validate fallback routing keeps p95 success rate >90%.

ravi: I'm running the replay in staging now. initial run shows same pattern: scale starts but worker init takes ~30-45s => headroom needed.

brightline-sre: if we increase burst credits now will that retroactively allow the previously dropped requests to be retried? or do we need the client to retry?

luke: clients need to retry. dropped requests are not retried server-side. We can reduce 429s going forward by increasing credits / headroom / routing, but clients should implement exponential backoff. add guidance: retry-after header present on 429s.

jessica: action items / owners: 1) luke — enable hosted fallback routing (in 10m) 2) ravi/emma — run canary config for headroom + aggressive scaling and validate in staging (today) 3) jessica — contact Brightline PM to schedule quota/billing change for burst credits trial and notify account exec. 4) billing-bot — prepare one-off 24h trial credit for Brightline pending approval.

billing-bot: prepared internal approval request link: https://redwood.internal/billing/req/BR-7892 (please review).

brightline-sre: thanks. we'll also add client-side retry logic and rate-limit before sending to Redwood to smooth the burst. appreciate the quick triage.

emma: postmortem notes draft: "Root cause: insufficient burst credit + autoscale latency led to admission control rejecting requests during marketing-driven traffic burst. Mitigations: increase default headroom for marketing-prone pools, reduce worker init latency, provide guidance and temporary burst credit trials to customers."

jessica: closing loop — I'll follow up once we confirm canary results and billing for trial credits. :white_check_mark:
